subtitle: Spain and France sit atop the field as co-leaders due to their combination of recent major-tournament success, squad depth, and attacking talent, with Spain benefiting from Euro 2024 title-winning form and players like Lamine Yamal while France draws on 2018 and 2022 pedigree under Didier Deschamps. England follows closely on the back of consistent qualification results and strong recent friendlies, though all three remain tightly grouped because of the expanded 48-team format and multiple high-caliber European sides capable of navigating the group stage and knockout rounds. Argentina and Brazil maintain realistic paths through defending-champion experience and historical pedigree, while Germany and Portugal round out the next tier on the strength of qualifying dominance and star availability. The bunched probabilities reflect a genuinely open race where small shifts in form, fitness, or matchups could reorder the hierarchy before the June 11 kickoff.
